# sutramx_escalation_policies (Data Source)

Escalation policies of the workspace, newest first. Read-only: policies reroute alerts, so the API only lets the workspace owner create or change them from the dashboard, not with API keys. Creating policies needs a plan that includes escalation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Escalation policies are created in the dashboard by the workspace owner;
# Terraform can look them up by name.
data "sutramx_escalation_policies" "primary" {
  name = "Primary on-call"
}

output "primary_policy_id" {
  value = one(data.sutramx_escalation_policies.primary.policies[*].id)
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `name` (String) Only policies with exactly this name.

### Read-Only

- `policies` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policies))

<a id="nestedatt--policies"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policies`

Read-Only:

- `enabled` (Boolean)
- `id` (String)
- `max_depth` (Number) How many steps an incident escalates through at most.
- `name` (String)
- `steps` (Attributes List) Steps in escalation order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--policies--steps))

<a id="nestedatt--policies--steps"></a>
### Nested Schema for `policies.steps`

Read-Only:

- `channel` (String) Delivery channel, e.g. `email`, `slack`, `webhook`.
- `delay_minutes` (Number) Minutes after the previous step before this one notifies.
- `id` (String)
- `step_order` (Number)
- `target_label` (String) Human-readable target, as shown in the dashboard.
- `target_type` (String) `email`, `on_call_primary`, `phone` or `integration`.
- `target_value` (String) Address, number or integration connection id the step notifies.
